newsitem.title: HONG KONG: FOCUS - HK Telecom deal under no political pressure.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - HK Telecom deal under no political pressure.

text.p: Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd said on Friday that political pressure did not figure in a major shareholder's decision to sell part of Hongkong Telecom to China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (MPT).

Hongkong Telecom's 59.2 percent shareholder Cable & Wireless signed an agreement on Friday with MPT's China Telecom (HK) Corp, to sell 5.5 percent of Hongkong Telecom for a total of HK$9.177 billion (US$1.185 billion) to China Telecom.
China Telecom is controlled by Telpo Communications Development Ltd, an MPT holding company in Hong Kong.
"Cable & Wireless and Hongkong Telecom have never been under any political pressure to get into any deal," Linus Cheung, Hongkong Telecom chief executive, told a news conference.
A Cable & Wireless spokesman said: "This has been from day one a commercial discussion."
Wu Jichuan, China's Minister for Posts and Telecommunications, said in a statement that the agreement was reached "on the basis of mutual benefit."
Cheung said the HK$14.25 a share price paid by China Telecom represented its average close for the past 30 trading days.
Cable & Wireless chief executive Richard Brown said Cable & Wireless and China Telecom were forging a long-term alliance to develop telecommunication operations in China and Hong Kong.
Cheung said the deal was a "win, win, win, win" situation for Hongkong Telecom, Cable & Wireless, MPT and Hong Kong.
He added that China Telecom and Hongkong Telecom might in future invest in overseas ventures jointly.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty on July 1, but China has agreed to let Hong Kong keep to its free market ways for 50 years under a "one country-two systems" compromise.

The deal "clearly demonstrates that China is pragmatic and China is keen to honour one country-two systems and to protect the interests of all the investors in Hong Kong," Cheung said. Under the deal, Cable & Wireless said it was prepared to transfer more shares "in expectation of Cable & Wireless and China Telecom becoming equal shareholders in Hongkong Telecom."
Recent speculation of a deal with MPT or another Chinese company has helped send Hongkong Telecom shares spiralling, culminating in Friday's record close at HK$19.00 a share.
The China Telecom pact is the latest in a series of Chinese companies taking strategic stakes in key Hong Kong firms.
China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd, controlled by China's State Council, said this week that a unit had signed a US$1.05 billion bridging loan to part-finance a Hongkong Telecom stake.
China Everbright had earlier agreed to pay HK$12.60 a share or a total of HK$11.4 billion for 7.74 percent of Hongkong Telecom from CITIC Pacific Ltd.
China Everbright is one of 16 equal shareholders in China United Telecommunications Corp, China's second largest telecom provider and a rival of MPT.
CITIC Pacific holds 20 percent of China Light & Power Co Ltd, one of Hong Kong's two power providers and also controls 25 percent of Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd.
China National Aviation Corp, an arm of China's aviation regulator, the Civil Aviation Authority of China, holds just over 35 percent of Hong Kong Dragaon Airlines Ltd.
